Generality is mostly strong: applicability/use_when state the pattern as a conjunction P∧Q over a shared hypothesis context, the README answers the bounded-prover question ('one hole per conjunct, each a self-contained statement'; leaves are self-contained because each closes from shared step1 and never its sibling), and most consequences are honest. But the 'avoid_when'/consequences overstate the uniformity requirement, and the entry's own example refutes it: step2 takes FOUR assumptions (hReg hBasis hCLF hClosed, lines 4626-4630) while step3 takes THREE, yet the parent applies both with a uniform [OF hReg hBasis hCLF] (lines 5070-5071) and argo still closes, discharging step2's residual hClosed premise. So 'the whole glue depends on both children taking exactly the same assumes in the same order' and 'a child that adds ... a hypothesis breaks the [OF hReg hBasis hCLF] template' are false as written. Fix: state that the SHARED hypotheses must form a common prefix in the same order, and that a child may append extra assumptions (like step2's hClosed), which surface as a residual premise for the glue's automation — what breaks the template is reordering/renaming/dropping one of the shared prefix, or adding a hypothesis before it.
